rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that something is only or just the case.

example.english: I merely want to have a cup of coffee.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zing6 hai6 soeng2 jam2 bui1 gaa3 fe1

rows.note: Use this when merely limits or softens an action, opinion, or situation rather than stressing strict numerical exclusivity.

example.english: I was merely asking; you don't have to get so angry.
example.traditional: 我只係問吓啫，你唔使咁嬲。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zi2 hai6 man6 haa5 ze1 nei5 m4 sai2 gam3 nau1

rows.note: Choose this when downplaying something as nothing more than a particular fact or circumstance.

example.english: This is merely a small matter.
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 si6 zi2 bat1 gwo3 hai6 siu2 si6

rows.note: Use this when merely means that an action has no other motive or ulterior reason.

example.english: I merely want to help you; I have no other motive.
example.traditional: 我純粹想幫你，冇其他意思。
example.jyutping: ngo5 seon4 seoi6 soeng2 bong1 nei5 mou5 kei4 taa1 ji3 si1
